g.text: 901 people estimated the same nine dot counts. Higher score means a more accurate panel.
Match the score of 10 typed responses; read each format's equivalent panel size at its first crossing.
Fractional k: linear interpolation in expected score.
The next page reports whole-person thresholds.
Score = negative expected squared error; zero is perfect. Straight segments connect exact finite-pool scores at k = 1-100.
Paper-style crossings applied to known truths; no fitted logarithm or extrapolation. Source: arXiv:2106.01254v3, Sec. 5.3.
Source: Honda, Kagawa & Shirasuna (2022) | Data: osf.io/sxdf9 | Analysis: 23 Sep 2026
